# NovaMart: the synthetic demonstration dataset

**NovaMart is a fictional retailer.** Every NovaMart record is generated by AUREX from a fixed random seed. NovaMart is not
DMart (Avenue Supermarts), MR D.I.Y., Wellness Forever or any other real business, and the dataset contains no real company
data ([novamart_generator.py:1-5](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L1-L5)). Supplier, landlord, bank and brand
names carry "(fictional)"; store names are invented, the cities are real places in Maharashtra.

AUREX separately ships cited public reference data about real retailers (DMart, MR D.I.Y., Wellness Forever, MedPlus, Vishal Mega Mart, 99 Speed Mart) for company intelligence and benchmarking
([data/reference/companies.json](../backend/app/data/reference/companies.json), loaded by
[seed/reference.py](../backend/app/seed/reference.py)) and integration-catalogue profiles of the POS/ERP vendors named in the
project brief ([registry.py](../backend/app/connectors/registry.py)). Neither is part of NovaMart, and benchmarking labels the
own-company row as synthetic and not comparable ([intelligence.py](../backend/app/services/intelligence.py) `benchmark`).

Code: [seed/novamart_generator.py](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py) (simulation),
[connectors/synthetic.py](../backend/app/connectors/synthetic.py) (feeds), [seed/demo.py](../backend/app/seed/demo.py) (demo
organization).

## 2. Reproducibility

- `NovaMartConfig` (frozen dataclass): `seed = 20231001`, `start = 2023-10-01`, `end = 2026-10-17`, all stores and
  categories, 8 products per category, daily snapshots for the last 120 days, INR, fiscal year from April, opening cash
  INR 85,000,000 ([novamart_generator.py:161-172](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L161-L172)).
- The demo feeds take the seed and end date from `AUREX_DEMO_SEED` / `AUREX_DEMO_END_DATE` (defaults `20231001`,
  `2026-10-17`) unless the integration config overrides them ([synthetic.py:36-44](../backend/app/connectors/synthetic.py#L36-L44),
  [config.py:99-100](../backend/app/core/config.py#L99-L100)).
- One `numpy.random.default_rng(seed)` drives a single simulation that produces every feed, so all figures are mutually
  consistent ([novamart_generator.py:7-10](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L7-L10), [novamart_generator.py:215-217](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L215-L217)).
- `cached_generate` memoizes the generated dataset per configuration (`lru_cache(maxsize=4)`), so every feed and both demo
  syncs reuse one simulation per process ([novamart_generator.py:887-889](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L887-L889)).

[novamart_generator.py:110-143](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L110-L143):

| Code | Name | Gross margin | Price elasticity | Price range (INR) | Refund rate | Supplier | Cover / safety days | Trend per year |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STAPLES | Staples | 17% | -0.45 | 60-650 | 0.3% | SUP-AGRO (SKUs 002/004/006/008: SUP-MILL) | 25 / 5 | 5% |
| PRODUCE | Fresh Produce | 26% | -0.8 | 30-200 | 0.4% | SUP-FRESH | 3 / 1 | 7% |
| DAIRY | Dairy & Eggs | 16% | -0.5 | 25-600 | 0.2% | SUP-DAIRY | 4 / 1 | 6% |
| SNACKS | Packaged Foods & Snacks | 27% | -1.2 | 20-350 | 0.4% | SUP-SNACK | 30 / 6 | 8% |
| BEVERAGES | Beverages | 28% | -1.4 | 20-450 | 0.3% | SUP-BEV | 25 / 5 | 9% |
| PCARE | Personal Care | 32% | -1.1 | 80-400 | 1.0% | SUP-CARE | 40 / 7 | 8% |
| HOMECARE | Home Care | 29% | -1.0 | 90-550 | 0.8% | SUP-HOME | 40 / 7 | 7% |
| KITCHEN | Home & Kitchen | 36% | -1.6 | 150-1500 | 2.5% | SUP-KITCH | 50 / 10 | 10% |
| APPAREL | Apparel Basics | 42% | -1.8 | 150-900 | 4.5% | SUP-TEX | 50 / 10 | 11% |
| ELECTRONICS | Electronics Accessories | 21% | -2.0 | 120-1600 | 3.0% | SUP-TECH | 120 / 10 | 12% |

Products ([novamart_generator.py:224-239](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L224-L239)): 8 named products per category
(80 in total), SKU `NM-<first four letters of the category code>-<001..008>` (e.g. `NM-STAP-001`, `NM-ELEC-003`); price
log-uniform in the category range rounded to INR 5; product margin = category margin + Normal(0, 0.025), clipped to 6-60%;
product elasticity = category elasticity x Uniform(0.85, 1.15).

Suppliers ([novamart_generator.py:96-108](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L96-L108)), contracted lead time / SD /
delay factor / payment terms: SUP-AGRO 4 d / 0.8 / 1.0 / 30 d; SUP-MILL 5 / 1.0 / 1.05 / 30; SUP-FRESH 1 / 0.3 / 1.0 / 7;
SUP-DAIRY 1 / 0.3 / 1.0 / 15; SUP-SNACK 5 / 1.2 / 1.1 / 30; SUP-BEV 4 / 0.9 / 1.0 / 30; SUP-CARE 6 / 1.3 / 1.0 / 45;
SUP-HOME 6 / 1.2 / 1.15 / 45; SUP-KITCH 10 / 2.5 / 1.2 / 45; SUP-TEX 9 / 2.0 / 1.1 / 60; SUP-TECH 8 / 2.0 / 1.0 / 45. A
purchase order's actual lead time is Normal(lead x delay factor, SD), rounded and clipped to 1-40 days
([novamart_generator.py:419-426](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L419-L426)).

## 5. Demand drivers

Daily demand per store x product ([novamart_generator.py:344-354](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L344-L354)) is
Poisson-Gamma distributed around

`base units x 0.85 x seasonality x weekday x price effect x promotion effect x (1 + marketing lift) x store factor x ramp x shock x noise`

| Driver | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Weekday | Mon..Sun 0.93, 0.88, 0.90, 0.95, 1.05, 1.20, 1.24 | [L149](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L149) |
| Festivals | Diwali 2023-11-12, 2024-11-01, 2025-10-21, 2026-11-08 (20 days before to 2 after, category uplift 8% Produce to 95% Apparel); Ganesh Chaturthi 2023-09-19, 2024-09-07, 2025-08-27, 2026-09-14 (7 before to 3 after, +12%, Produce +18% more) | [L145-148](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L145-L148), [L249-258](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L249-L258) |
| Season | Mid-May summer peak (Beverages +38%, Dairy +12%), late-July monsoon dip (-6%), salary week (day <= 7) Staples +8%, 24-31 December Snacks and Beverages +10% | [L251-268](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L251-L268) |
| Trend | (1 + category trend)^years | [L269-270](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L269-L270) |
| Prices | Annual cost (+2-5%, 10-40 days early) and price (+2-5%) revisions on 1 April 2024, 2025, 2026; one or two permanent product price tests of -8/-5/+5/+8%; demand reacts to the real price index (deflated by 5% a year) with the product elasticity | [L282-297](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L282-L297), [L346-347](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L346-L347) |
| Promotions | Weekly per product with probability 7% (17% in festive weeks), depth 8-25%; effect (1 - depth)^elasticity x 1.05 | [L303-306](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L303-L306), [L348](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L348) |
| Marketing | Weekly spend INR 34,000 x open stores x (1 + 1.2 x festive intensity) x lognormal noise over five channels; lift = 7.5% x adstock / (adstock + half-saturation), adstock decay 0.55 | [L308-324](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L308-L324) |
| Store ramp | 1 - 0.45 e^(-months open / 4.5) | [L335](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L335) |

Sales are demand capped by stock on hand (stockouts lose sales), and replenishment follows a reorder-point policy: when
on hand + on order falls to the planner's trailing 28-day demand x (lead time + safety days), an order up to that point plus
cover days is placed, rounded to case packs, one purchase order per store, supplier and day
([novamart_generator.py:366-431](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L366-L431)). Refunds are binomial at the category
refund rate and are restocked for the non-food categories; Produce and Dairy lose 4% of stock to weekly spoilage
(`write_off` movements).

## 6. Embedded storylines

The generator builds operating stories into the data so that the analytics have something real to find, without
hard-coding answers ([novamart_generator.py:12-19](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L12-L19)):

| Storyline | Mechanism | Where it should surface |
|---|---|---|
| S04 loses demand to a competitor | Demand x 0.84 from 2026-02-01 ([L336-337](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L336-L337)); monthly customer retention drops from about 62% to 55% ([L737-738](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L737-L738)) | Store growth and contribution, revenue bridge by store (transactions vs basket), customer retention |
| S04 keeps a fixed 20-person roster | Headcount pinned to the base headcount 20 and no festive extra staff ([L511-514](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L511-L514)); departments 9 + 6 + 3 + 2 | Labour cost % and transactions per labour hour worsen at S04; Decision Lab finds S04 not capacity-constrained, so extra staff adds cost only (the 20 to 30 test, [DECISION_LAB.md](DECISION_LAB.md#11-the-required-test-20-to-30-employees)) |
| Beverage supplier delay in peak season | SUP-BEV mean lead time tripled for orders placed 2026-04-01 to 2026-05-31 ([L424-425](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L424-L425)), coinciding with the beverage summer peak | Supplier lead-time alert, beverage stockout risk, category decline in the revenue bridge, the advisor's supply check |
| Electronics over-ordered | Cover target 120 days, against 3-50 days for the other categories ([L139-142](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L139-L142)) | Overstock list and excess value, low inventory turnover |
| Staples margin squeeze | Staples costs +6% on 2025-07-01, prices +3% only on 2025-10-01 ([L288-290](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L288-L290)) | Staples gross margin dip, July-September 2025 |
| New stores ramp up | S07 (2024-07-12) and S08 (2025-11-01) follow the ramp; capex INR 38,000,000 and 41,000,000 paid over the three months before opening, pre-opening rent, payroll and INR 650,000 other costs ([L583-598](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L583-L598), [L767-774](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L767-L774)) | Non-comparable store growth, the Decision Lab's fitted ramp and capex per sq ft |
| S08 cost data missing | `cost_amount` NULL (unknown, not zero) for S08's first 61 days, a "POS migration" ([L447-451](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L447-L451)) | Cost coverage below 100% in those months; gross profit estimated or withheld by the P&L coverage rules |
| Marketing experiments | Spend x 0.4 in January 2025 and x 1.8 in June 2025 ([L314-318](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L314-L318)) | An identifiable marketing elasticity (the true adstock decay 0.55 is one of the calibration grid values) |
| S01 refurbishment | Demand x 0.70 from 2025-01-06 to 2025-01-19, x 1.05 afterwards ([L338-341](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L338-L341)); INR 12,000,000 capex in December 2024 and extra depreciation over 84 months from February 2025 ([L611-612](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L611-L612), [L775-777](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L775-L777)) | S01 January 2025 dip, investing cash flow, depreciation step |
| Price tests | Random permanent product price changes ([L291-295](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L291-L295)) | Identified category price elasticities in the Decision Lab |

Other modelled facts ([novamart_generator.py:494-844](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L494-L844)): monthly workforce
by store department (Sales Floor 45%, Front End 30%, Warehouse 15%, Management 10%; hourly rates by department and city,
4% annual wage growth, 15% employer on-cost, 2x overtime premium, 200 hours per employee per month, 3.5% monthly
separations) plus 21 head-office staff (one more in IT and in Merchandising from June 2025); ledger expenses booked at month
end (rent x 1.2 escalating 5% per fiscal year, utilities with a summer peak, logistics 1.8% and store supplies 0.5% of sales,
head-office costs, marketing accrued from the spend feed); a term loan of INR 80,000,000 at 9.6% with INR 1,000,000 monthly
repayments and a INR 35,000,000 drawdown in August 2025; income tax at 25.17% of positive quarterly profit, booked in
quarter-end months; supplier payments lagged by payment terms; month-end bank balances; FY2026 and FY2027 "Annual Budget"
versions (prior-year month x 1.09, new stores at 70% of the mature average). Inventory snapshots are weekly (Sundays) for the
whole history plus daily for the last 120 days ([L711](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L711)).

## 7. Feeds and integrations created by the demo seed

`SyntheticDemoConnector` serves one feed per integration ([synthetic.py:25-32](../backend/app/connectors/synthetic.py#L25-L32)):

| Feed | Integration display name | Entities |
|---|---|---|
| `erp` | NovaMart ERP · synthetic demo feed | store, category, supplier, product, department, purchase_order, purchase_order_line, inventory_movement, inventory_snapshot, budget |
| `pos` | NovaMart POS · synthetic demo feed | sales (daily summary per store x SKU), traffic, customer_metric |
| `accounting` | NovaMart Accounting · synthetic demo feed | expense, cash_flow, cash_balance |
| `hris` | NovaMart HRIS · synthetic demo feed | workforce (aggregates, no personal data) |
| `marketing` | NovaMart Marketing · synthetic demo feed | marketing_spend (weekly by channel) |

The ERP integration is created first because it supplies the dimensions the others reference ([demo.py:38-45](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L38-L45)).
All five start `connected` with config `{feed, small, lookback_days: 3, as_of}` ([demo.py:126-137](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L126-L137)).
The feed can be read "as of" a date: dated facts up to `as_of`, and with a cursor only rows after `cursor.through - lookback`;
purchase orders received after `as_of` are reported as still open without a received date
([synthetic.py:76-127](../backend/app/connectors/synthetic.py#L76-L127)). The seed runs the real pipeline twice per integration
([demo.py:151-170](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L151-L170)):

1. **Initial load** (`trigger = seed`) as of `end - 7 days`.
2. **Incremental sync** (`trigger = schedule`) as of `end` with the 3-day lookback: the overlapping days arrive again and are
   counted as unchanged, and orders received in the final week arrive as updates.

**Example REST integration awaiting credentials.** "Supplier portal API (example, awaiting credentials)", provider
`generic_rest`, status `awaiting_credentials`, base URL `https://api.supplier-portal.example/v1`, API-key header auth, test
endpoint `/me`, no entities. Nothing is ever synced; it exists to show an integration that is not live and says so
([demo.py:138-148](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L138-L148)).

**Invalid-CSV example.** "Manual sales corrections (CSV)" (`csv_upload`, entity `sales`) receives
`sales_corrections_<date>.csv`, uploaded as the business-analyst user through the real file-import path, with the dates set to
the day before the last data date ([demo.py:54-63](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L54-L63), [demo.py:187-221](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L187-L221)).
It exists so that sync history, rejected rows, error codes and statuses are demonstrated honestly. On the full dataset:

| Row | Content | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `S01, NM-STAP-001`, valid | Loaded |
| 2 | store `S99` | Rejected: `unknown_store` |
| 3 | SKU `NM-UNKNOWN-1` | Rejected: `unknown_product` |
| 4 | date written `dd/mm/yyyy` (`16/10/2026` with the default end date) | Rejected: `invalid_date` (no `date_format` configured; non-ISO dates are never guessed) |
| 5 | quantity `-4` | Rejected: `negative_value` |
| 6 | gross 500, discount 50, net 400 | Rejected: `net_mismatch` |
| 7 | quantity `two` | Rejected: `invalid_number` |
| 8 | `cost_amount` blank | Loaded with cost NULL (unknown, not zero) |

The job ends `partially_succeeded`. With `--small` only three SKUs per category exist, so rows 6-8 fail on `unknown_product`
as well and only row 1 loads. Because this integration is created after the POS feed and no authority rule names it, the
POS feed remains the system of record for S01 on that day: the correction rows are stored but not counted, and the store-day
shows two overlapping sources ([DATA_MODEL.md](DATA_MODEL.md#5-system-of-record-and-agg_store_daily)).

The seed also creates fiscal periods from FY2023 to two years past the end date ([demo.py:116](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L116)),
and `main()` loads the public reference data ([demo.py:250-256](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L250-L256)).

## 8. Demo users

One user per role ([demo.py:47-52](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L47-L52), [demo.py:66-69](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L66-L69),
[demo.py:118-124](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L118-L124)):

| Role | E-mail | Name | Store scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org_owner` | demo.org-owner@novamart.example | Riya Owner (demo) | all |
| `executive` | demo.executive@novamart.example | Arjun CEO (demo) | all |
| `finance_manager` | demo.finance-manager@novamart.example | Meera Finance (demo) | all |
| `operations_manager` | demo.operations-manager@novamart.example | Kabir Operations (demo) | S01, S02 |
| `inventory_manager` | demo.inventory-manager@novamart.example | Sana Inventory (demo) | all |
| `hr_manager` | demo.hr-manager@novamart.example | Dev HR (demo) | all |
| `business_analyst` | demo.business-analyst@novamart.example | Isha Analyst (demo) | all |
| `employee` | demo.employee@novamart.example | Omkar Employee (demo) | S04 |
| `auditor` | demo.auditor@novamart.example | Neha Auditor (demo) | all |
| `platform_admin` | demo.platform@aurex.example | Platform Admin (demo) | not a member of the organization |

- Store scopes are set after the stores exist ([demo.py:173-181](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L173-L181)); with `--small` S02 does
  not exist, so the operations manager is scoped to S01 only.
- Demo users are passwordless in practice: the stored hash is of a random, undisclosed token
  ([demo.py:85-94](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L85-L94)), and password sign-in rejects `is_demo` users
  ([auth.py:222](../backend/app/services/auth.py#L222)). They sign in only through `POST /api/v1/auth/demo/login` with
  `{"role": "<role>"}`; `GET /api/v1/auth/demo/roles` lists the seeded roles. Both require `AUREX_DEMO_MODE=true`
  ([routes/auth.py:170-211](../backend/app/api/routes/auth.py#L170-L211)). Demo users cannot change passwords or create
  organizations.
- Production refuses to start with demo mode on unless `AUREX_ALLOW_DEMO_IN_PRODUCTION=true`, intended for a showcase that
  holds only synthetic data ([config.py:141-143](../backend/app/core/config.py#L141-L143)).

## 9. `small_config()` for tests

[novamart_generator.py:892-897](../backend/app/seed/novamart_generator.py#L892-L897): stores S01 and S04; categories STAPLES,
BEVERAGES and ELECTRONICS with 3 products each; 2025-10-01 to 2026-04-30; daily snapshots for the last 30 days. The S04
competitor shock (February 2026), the fixed S04 roster and the Electronics cover target fall inside this window. A demo
integration with `small: true` always uses this window, whatever `AUREX_DEMO_END_DATE` says
([synthetic.py:36-44](../backend/app/connectors/synthetic.py#L36-L44)). The test session seeds it with
`seed_demo(db, small=True)`, loads the reference data and trains company and S04 net-sales forecasts
([conftest.py:68-76](../backend/tests/conftest.py#L68-L76)).

## 10. Commands

Run from `backend/` against a migrated database:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `python -m app.seed.demo` | Create (or top up) the demo organization and run both syncs on the full dataset |
| `python -m app.seed.demo --small` | Same with `small_config()` (quick demos, tests) |
| `python -m app.seed.demo --reset` | Delete the demo organization (fact rows first, because integrations are `ON DELETE RESTRICT`) and every demo user, then seed again |
| `python -m app.seed.demo --train` | After seeding, train the default forecast plan: company targets, every store, every category ([FORECASTING.md](FORECASTING.md#8-default-plan-and-retraining)) |
| `docker compose run --rm seed` | The compose `seed` service (profile `demo`) runs `python -m app.seed.demo --train` ([docker-compose.yml:154-157](../docker-compose.yml#L154-L157)) |

After seeding (and before any training) `main()` runs `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` on the bulk-loaded fact tables and
`agg_store_daily`, so planner statistics are fresh before first use ([demo.py:224-239](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L224-L239),
[demo.py:262-264](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L262-L264)); `seed_demo()` called directly, as the test suite does, skips it.

Flags combine (`--reset --small --train`). Sources: [demo.py:242-278](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L242-L278),
[demo.py:72-82](../backend/app/seed/demo.py#L72-L82). Seeding is idempotent for the organization, users and integrations:
existing rows are reused, re-delivered facts are counted as unchanged, and the CSV example is skipped if the same file was
